text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up on continuous batching scheduler — tradeoffs for queueing. TL;DR: need to pick a primary objective (tail latency SLO vs GPU utilization vs fairness) and an operational model for backpressure. Thoughts?

jon: +1. current prototype (time-window + size threshold) improved GPU utilization but p99 shot up for some tenants. we need a hybrid approach.

nina: Can you share the numbers? small summary helps.

maria: Sure. experiment A: window=8ms, max_batch_tokens=4096 -> throughput +12% but p99 increased ~300ms for 3/50 tenants (those with long prompts). logs: 
```
scheduler.stats: {avg_batch_size: 28, avg_wait_ms: 6.2, p99_wait_ms: 45, backlog_len: 32}
request.latency: {tenant:a: p99=740ms, tenant:b: p99=220ms}
```

kevin: Head-of-line blocking. long prompt sits at head, subsequent short requests wait until batch fills or timeout.

jon: Options I see: 1) per-tenant queues + WFQ/DRR to guarantee share, 2) size-based sub-queues (short vs long), 3) preemption: flush short requests ahead if stuck.

nina: Preemption worries me — complexity and correctness with KV cache. If you preempt, you might need to split KV cache state between partial batches. tricky.

maria: Good point. We considered split-batches where a long request can be split into head tokens (fast path) + tail (background). but that requires model support for resuming context across workers.

kevin: Could we adopt a priority lane for short requests: detect requests with expected tokens <= 64 and keep a micro-batcher (window 2ms) for them? Materially reduces p99 for short ones without hurting long ones.

jon: That seems pragmatic. But we must avoid starvation: when short-lane is saturated it should borrow capacity from main pool. Also enforcement: how do we count token budget? per-request expected_tokens header? best-effort estimator?

maria: We already surface `approx_token_count` in client SDK. Could make scheduler use it for lane selection. fallback: request-level hint or dynamic heuristic (first N tokens length).

nina: For fairness we should add a deficit counter per tenant so multi-tenant customers can't monopolize short-lane. DRR with two priority classes (short/long) per tenant.

kevin: Agreed. Implementation sketch:
```
queues = {tenant_id: {short_queue: deque(), long_queue: deque(), deficit: 0}}
while true:
  for t in active_tenants:
    deficit[t] += quantum
    while deficit[t] >= cost(peek(t)):
      req = pop_preferred_queue(t)  # prefer short_queue
      schedule(req)
      deficit[t] -= cost(req)
```
cost(req) = max(1, approx_tokens/64)
quantum tuned to target throughput per tenant
```

maria: Nice. Also consider multi-queue eviction policy: if global backlog > N, start shedding low-priority or rate-limit tenant shares (503 fast) instead of letting latency spiral.

jon: We should simulate worst-case: bursty small requests + a few huge long-continuations. can we run a cheap event-driven sim to measure p50/p99/instability?

nina: I can add a sim. need input distributions: short: 80% (1-64 tokens, exp(10)), medium: 15% (64-512), long: 5% (>512 heavy-tail). per-tenant skew: top 10% tenants generate 60% traffic.

kevin: Also track KV cache effectiveness: batching with mixed sequences hurts cache locality. metric: cache_hit_rate, kv_payload_size. if short-lane improves hit rate, it's a win.

maria: Ops question: how to expose config? runtime flags per-deployment + per-customer overrides? I'd rather default to safe global heuristics and allow per-tenant tuning via Dedicated config.

jon: Default + opt-in per-tenant tuning seems fine. For hosted: enable short-lane + DRR with conservative quantum. Dedicated customers can tune.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: continuous-batcher/v2 -> staging (maria) at 2024-04-18T15:20:00Z :rocket:

maria: Next steps I propose: 1) nina builds sim and shares p50/p95/p99 for candidate schedulers, 2) kevin implements short-lane + DRR prototype, 3) jon writes canary plan and SLOs (p50/p95/p99 per-lane), 4) ops doc for rate-shed thresholds.

jon: Add a metric: `batch.mixed_request_fraction` to monitor mixed-length batches. if > X% we flip to more aggressive short-lane sizing.

nina: I'll start the sim tonight and post results. expect PR with sim code + plots.

kevin: I'll prototype the queue structures; aim for safe default toggles and a feature flag for canary.

maria: Great. please keep the RFC thread updated with sim results. tagging @sre-bot for alert tuning once we can measure sensible thresholds. :thumbsup:
